svg.title: Annex A6 · News and alerts: reading, filtering, history and place
svg.desc: News and alerts in the daily run: download, tolerant parsing, relevance and hazard filter, append-only history with its copy, and UBIGEO placement with the console's corrections.
svg.text: Annex A6 · News and alerts: reading, filtering, history and place

Every run reads 168 feeds, keeps the notes about El Niño or about a hazard in Peru, appends them to a history that never deletes and places each one in its department, province and district. Reviewers fix the place in the console
Details these boxes of the full diagram: News and alerts: reading and filtering, Append-only news history, Placement and place corrections.
8 threads · serial per server · 60 s per feed

g.title: 1. 168 feeds → Reader feeds: forbidden by robots.txt. Reader feeds follow their own pace; the rest are requested every run.
2. Reader feeds → Feed download: when due. If 20 h have not passed since the last request, they are not requested and their previous state stays.
3. 168 feeds → Feed download: 128 feeds every run. One after another per server, out of courtesy; 10 minutes to start them all.
4. Feed download → Status of each feed: result per feed. A feed with no new entries for a long time is marked inactive.
5. Feed download → Tolerant parsing: news feeds. XML, JSON or HTML as they arrived.
6. Feed download → Alerts without RSS: alert sources. Each alert source with its own format.
7. Tolerant parsing → Relevance: entries. Headline, summary, date and link.
8. Alerts without RSS → Relevance: alerts with place. Alerts bring their place and severity from the source.
9. Relevance → 13 hazard types: relevant notes. Only those that pass the filter.
10. 13 hazard types → Append only: new notes. A note already seen is not added again.
11. Published history → Append only: previous history. The base the new notes are appended to.
12. Copy in data-archive → Append only: missing notes or rebuild. news-history-restored if it adds notes; news-history-missing if it has to rebuild.
13. Append only → Placement (UBIGEO): the whole history. Everything is placed again with the current rules: an improvement also applies to old notes.
14. Placement (UBIGEO) → Console corrections: automatic place. With its method, confidence and evidence.
15. Console corrections → What gets published: final place. The correction with the highest revision wins.
16. What gets published → Note clusters: placed notes. Clusters are built from recent notes.
168 feeds. 116 media and government feeds, 38 Google News searches and 14 alert sources, with the registry's plan.

g.title: Feed download. Its own client with shorter waits than the official one: 2 tries, 1 s between requests to the same server, 60 s per feed. If a feed fails, it uses the newest Peru or n8n copy. Technology: httpx, Fetcher.

g.title: Append only. Appends the new notes (id = hash of link and headline) and never rewrites earlier ones; CSV protected against formulas. warning at 20 MiB. Technology: JSON Lines, CSV.

g.title: Placement (UBIGEO). By the source's fields, by coordinates (point in polygon on IGN boundaries) or by the text (25 departments, 196 provinces, 1893 districts, with rules against false positives). Confidence 0.35 to 0.97. Technology: geo.py, limites.py.

If something fails: what happens and which fallback takes over
A feed does not answer or arrives broken
The newest Peru or n8n copy is used; if none, it shows as down in
news/feeds.json and the run goes on.
The previous notes and the latest known alerts are served; the 14 alert
sources show as unread, so silence does not look like calm.
The published history cannot be read
It is rebuilt from the data-archive copy; with no copy, only today's are
published marked restarted and the next run completes it.
A run requested the reader feeds and did not publish
Their state and notes stay in the Actions cache: the next run does not
request them before 20 h and keeps those notes.
The console does not answer or the site is on GitHub Pages
The corrections already published in geo/overrides.json are applied.
news-history-large warning at 20 MiB (Cloudflare serves up to 25 MiB per
file); the compressed copy stops growing, with a warning, before 90 MiB.
